title: Rancher v2.7.2 cattle-cluster-agent memory growth leads to OOM kills while using Explorer
body: I am running Rancher v2.7.2 as a Docker installation with Kubernetes 1.25. When I use the Rancher Explorer UI, cattle-cluster-agent memory keeps increasing and the pod is eventually OOM-killed. I expect its memory usage to remain stable.

symptoms_visible: When I use Rancher Explorer, the cattle-cluster-agent memory usage keeps increasing until the pod is OOM-killed.
N0.label: N0 cluster-agent memory growth reported

symptoms_visible: With an ad hoc memory limit, the cattle-cluster-agent still consumes memory until it restarts; the restart reclaims the memory.
N1_x.label: N1_x memory-limit workaround aftermath

symptoms_visible: The cattle-cluster-agent on hp-stg-cluster continues to grow in memory, and its logs repeatedly contain 'Unable to cancel request for *client.addQuery'.
Other affected environments also show sharply different cluster-agent memory growth after upgrading to Rancher 2.7.2.
N2.label: N2 affected cluster and diagnostics collected

symptoms_visible: After upgrading to Rancher 2.7.3 and adding the request-cache disable setting, the cluster-agent memory still increases.
N3_x.label: N3_x request-cache mitigation aftermath

symptoms_visible: The memory-growth problem remains, although there was not much growth occurring when I captured the requested heap profile.
N4.label: N4 heap snapshot collected

symptoms_visible: Maintainers and QA report stable memory with the goroutine fixes, but I have not reported a retest of the fixed release on my own affected cluster.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix shipped without reporter retest

solution.intent: Set a cattle-cluster-agent memory limit so Kubernetes restarts the pod before it exhausts the node.
solution.concrete_example: Patch the cattle-cluster-agent deployment with a finite memory request and limit; memory is reclaimed whenever the limited pod is restarted.

edges.comment: Reporter c1 and affected participants c10-c15/c35: memory limits reclaim memory through pod restarts and can protect the node, but memory continues growing. This is a temporary mitigation, not the leak fix.

question_patterns: Which cluster is affected, and how was that cluster created or imported?
Is the affected downstream cluster EKS, RKE, K3s, or another type?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It is currently happening on hp-stg-cluster. The cluster was created in AWS as EKS and then imported into Rancher.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It happens only on the local Rancher cluster and no downstream cattle-cluster-agent is involved.
The affected downstream cluster is imported RKE rather than imported EKS, but the same cluster-agent growth occurs.

question_patterns: Does the OOM behavior occur on every downstream cluster or only one of them?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: In my setup it is currently happening on hp-stg-cluster.

question_patterns: Can you share the cattle-cluster-agent logs from an affected cluster?
What messages appear in the cluster-agent logs while memory is increasing?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I pasted the cattle-cluster-agent log. It starts as Rancher agent v2.7.2 and contains many messages saying 'Unable to cancel request for *client.addQuery'.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The logs contain repeated kernel OOM messages but no request, watch, proxy, or addQuery errors.
The same addQuery cancellation message appears with different timestamps and pod names.

question_patterns: Can you download the downstream-cluster diagnostic data and share the Top 10 resources view?
Please provide Rancher diagnostic data and a screenshot of the largest resource counts.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I uploaded the Rancher diagnostic archive and this screenshot of the requested resource information.

question_patterns: Do you know whether many requests are being proxied to the downstream cluster through the Rancher API?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I don't know why there are so many requests.

question_patterns: Are other affected environments seeing the same growth after the upgrade?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. In another affected environment, RKE clusters on Ubuntu began showing the same steadily increasing cluster-agent memory after upgrading from 2.6.11 to 2.7.2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Only my imported EKS cluster shows it; no other deployment type has reproduced it.

edges.comment: Reporter c3-c7 supplies the hp-stg EKS details, logs, diagnostic archive, Top 10 screenshot, and uncertainty about proxy-request volume. Participant1 c0 is an affected operator whose RKE post-upgrade observation is folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Treat the growth as an unbounded Steve list-cache problem and disable the request cache on both Rancher and cattle-cluster-agent.
solution.concrete_example: Set CATTLE_REQUEST_CACHE_DISABLED=true on both the Rancher server and cattle-cluster-agent, or reduce CATTLE_REQUEST_CACHE_SIZE_INT if fully disabling the cache causes unacceptable API performance.

edges.comment: Participants c17-c18 proposed the list-cache hypothesis and environment-variable mitigation. Reporter c19 upgraded to 2.7.3 and reports that adding the cache-disable setting did not stop the memory growth, so it is falsified for the reporter's causal chain.

question_patterns: Can you collect a heap profile from the affected cattle-cluster-agent while its memory usage is high?
Please port-forward the agent's profiling port, download /debug/pprof/heap, and share the resulting file.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran the commands and uploaded heap.zip. I think there was not much memory growth occurring at the time the heap was created.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I captured profiles before and after the UI-triggered growth, and the second heap is dominated by a steadily retained cache allocation.
I collected the requested heap from another affected cattle-cluster-agent during another quiet period.

edges.comment: Reporter c21-c23 executes the requested pprof collection and supplies only the raw heap archive plus the timing caveat. The interpretation that this particular snapshot was flat and contained no large orphan allocation was made by participant6, not by the reporter.

solution.intent: Deploy a Rancher build containing the Steve goroutine-cleanup fixes, which terminate watch/proxy goroutines on unexpected error paths, and then verify memory stability on the affected cluster.
solution.concrete_example: Update to Rancher 2.7.5 or a later build containing the fixes validated in the 2.7.5 release candidate. The primary patch changes WatchNames error handling so goroutines terminate gracefully; a second goroutine issue was also resolved. After updating, exercise the same Explorer pages and monitor both Rancher and cattle-cluster-agent memory before declaring the incident resolved.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers reproduced growth by repeatedly refreshing resource-heavy Explorer pages and used goroutine profiles to identify Steve watch/proxy error paths, including returnErr and WatchNames handling. The reporter supplied logs and a heap captured during a quiet period; the goroutine diagnosis and QA validation are engineering conclusions, not facts the reporter produced.

edges.comment: Participants c37-c39 describe the test image, goroutine-profile signature, WatchNames error-handling patch, and QA validation. Participant10 c46 states that an additional goroutine issue was also fixed and that the release contains both fixes. No affected reporter subsequently confirms the fixed release on their own system, so terminal resolution remains unverified by the reporter.

solution.intent: Deploy a Rancher build containing the Steve goroutine-cleanup fixes and verify that Explorer activity no longer causes Rancher or cattle-cluster-agent memory to grow without bound.
solution.concrete_example: Use a fixed Rancher build rather than relying on OOM restarts or cache disabling, then reproduce the original Explorer workload while monitoring memory before considering the issue resolved.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents an agent proposing the thread's accepted goroutine fix immediately from the opening symptom. It skips the diagnostics and the two in-case mitigations that did not remove the underlying growth.

edges.comment: Shortcut required because the first actual move was the falsified memory-limit workaround. It allows an immediately correct proposal to match while explicitly recording the evidence it skips.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause as goroutines accumulating in Steve watch/proxy error paths because unexpected errors did not terminate them cleanly; the earlier list-cache hypothesis is not the accepted fix for the reporter's case.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the Explorer-associated memory growth, repeated addQuery cancellation messages, maintainer reproduction, and goroutine profiling rather than inferred from high memory usage alone.

Must recommend deploying a build containing both goroutine fixes and must not present CATTLE_REQUEST_CACHE_DISABLED as the reporter's resolution, because memory growth persisted after that setting and an upgrade.
Memory limits may be offered only as a temporary protection against node exhaustion; they cause periodic pod restarts and do not remove the underlying growth.
Must ask the reporter to repeat the affected Explorer workload and monitor Rancher and cattle-cluster-agent memory on a build containing the fix before declaring the reporter's environment resolved.
Must not claim that the original reporter verified the fix; the thread contains maintainer and QA validation but no reporter retest of the fixed release.

persona_hint.experience_level: Kubernetes and Rancher operator who can patch deployment resources, collect logs and diagnostics, upgrade Rancher, port-forward a pod, and capture a pprof heap, but relies on maintainers to interpret profiles and internal Rancher behavior.
persona_hint.communication_style: Brief and cooperative; answers numbered questions directly, uploads requested artifacts, asks for a workaround, and reports plainly when a proposed mitigation does not stop the memory growth.
